loci.name: google-tac-magnitude-repricing-and-appellate-tail
loci.one_line: What is Google TAC worth to Apple NOW, how fast does the court's non-exclusive annual-rebidding remedy compress its rate, and how fat is the appellate tail toward a payment ban inside the 2-5 year window?
loci.rationale: The only authoritative TAC figure is the court's ~$20B, explicitly 2022 and worldwide, set against FY2025 financials; the sole current estimate (Morgan Stanley >$25B at 95%+ margins) is one analyst of unclear geography. Both parties' experts agree price compresses under the remedy but no source quantifies speed or magnitude. The contradiction graph reclassified TAC as a repriceable annuity with 'two small binary tails' that are unquantified and undated; the only corpus note on the bilateral appeal (notices Feb 3 2026) lacks docket detail. TAC is ~10% of total and ~24% of Services gross profit, so this single number moves the falsification test more than any other.
loci.deliverable: (1) Defended RANGE for current annual TAC to Apple, with year, geography and method for each bound. (2) A rate-path range under non-exclusive annual rebidding over 2026-2031. (3) Appellate posture: who appealed what, grounds, briefing/argument timetable, and an evidence-based view of reversal-toward-ban likelihood — with the liability theory (exclusivity, not payment) weighed explicitly. Commit to a position.

opposing_positions.position: The appeal is unlikely to overturn payment permission: liability attached to the ISA's de facto exclusivity, not the payment mechanism itself; the court cited the pre-2005 non-exclusive default arrangement as a lawful less-restrictive counterfactual, so the remedies outcome was foreshadowed by the liability theory rather than being a lenient accident an appellate court is likely to reverse.

The tail is wider than 'small': DOJ (not only Google) appealed specifically because it considers the remedy too weak, its underlying ask (a full payment ban) is still on the table at the appellate level, Apple's own audited risk factors single out a DOJ-favourable reversal as a material adverse risk across three straight quarters, and the corpus itself records this posture only in a single low-authority press note with no docket detail -- an audited absence on exactly the question that determines the tail's true probability.

loci.name: appstore-commission-magnitude-margin-and-scotus-reversal
loci.one_line: What are App Store commission revenue and margin on court-surfaced evidence rather than one commercial estimator, and could the Supreme Court's review of the Epic contempt standard REVERSE the erosion now visible in reported numbers?
loci.rationale: Every commission-revenue figure traces to one estimator (Appfigures), restated across outlets. The ~90% margin used in the orchestrator's sizing is an explicit assumption with no evidence; the 2021 Epic trial disclosed App Store financials in findings of fact and those are absent from the corpus. Separately, SCOTUS granted cert June 30 2026 on the civil-contempt standard, staying district proceedings, but no note states the question presented or what follows if Apple wins — erosion could reverse, not merely pause. This locus supplies the second of the two numbers that carry the falsification test.
loci.deliverable: (1) Defended RANGE for global and US commission revenue, preferring court-surfaced figures (2021 Epic findings of fact) over commercial estimates. (2) An EVIDENCED commission margin range to replace the orchestrator's ~90% assumption. (3) The exact SCOTUS question presented, argument timing, and the commercial consequence of each outcome for US link-out commission. Commit to a position on whether erosion is durable.

opposing_positions.position: Commission erosion via steering is a realized, structural fact already visible in reported revenue (US commission revenue -18% YTD per Appfigures) and confirmed obliquely by Apple's own CFO -- the erosion should be modeled forward as continuing, with SCOTUS review as a minor procedural overhang.

SCOTUS granted cert specifically on the civil-contempt STANDARD used to hold Apple in contempt -- if the Court narrows or rejects that standard, the injunction's legal foundation (not merely its enforcement mechanics) could be undermined, which would let Apple reinstate a commission on external-link purchases and reverse the erosion the graph currently treats as a settled direction.

loci.name: ai-late-follower-chosen-vs-revealed
loci.one_line: Reader prior 1: is Apple's late-follower AI posture a chosen capital-allocation advantage, or a revealed execution failure now being managed capital-efficiently after the fact?
loci.rationale: This is the contradiction graph's own top dialectical candidate (cluster ai-late-follower-chosen-vs-revealed, rank 4, decision_relevance high), and it maps directly onto the query's mandated reader-prior test #1. The corpus contains a first-party admission that cuts against the 'chosen' framing: Craig Federighi stated the March 2025 Siri delay was caused by the V1 architecture failing to meet the quality bar, 'not a strategic choice' (apples-siri-revamp-reportedly-delayed-again-techcrunch), against ~18 months of repeated slippage (apple-reportedly-targets-spring-2026-for-launch-of-delayed-ai-siri-upgrade-but-i) and a cumulative 2020-2025 AI spend gap of ~$20B vs $141-205B for the hyperscalers (725b-on-ai-where-big-tech-is-spending-in-2026). Set against this: capex fell 19-28% YoY every FY2026 quarter while R&D rose 32-34%, explicitly tied to AI (aapl-20260627, aapl-20260328, aapl-20251227), a falling inference-cost curve (llm-inference-prices-have-fallen-rapidly-but-unequally-across-tasks-epoch-ai), and a market that rewarded Apple's restraint during the Feb 2026 hyperscaler capex selloff (660b-capex-bill-triggers-900b-wipeout-why-apple-shares-outperform-amazon-and-goo). The orchestrator's own synthesis calls this 'the strongest candidate for a dialectical locus' and proposes a split verdict (origin revealed, current management capital-efficient) — but that verdict was reached without depth investigation and needs testing against what has actually happened since (iOS 27 Siri launch reception, any post-Q3-FY26 capex/R&D data, and whether the market read of the Feb 2026 selloff holds up).
loci.deliverable: A committed verdict on the reader's prior that separates ORIGIN (chosen vs revealed) from CURRENT ECONOMICS (is renting capability capital-efficient now), grounded in Federighi's first-party statement, the FY2026 capex/R&D lines, the Gemini rental terms, and the persistence (not just the level) of inference-cost decline. Address whether the Sept 2026 iOS 27 Siri launch changes the picture.

opposing_positions.position: Chosen: deliberate capital discipline, renting capability (Gemini-powered Siri, ~$1B/yr) as inference costs collapse; capex fell 19-28% YoY every FY2026 quarter even as R&D rose ~33%, and markets rewarded the restraint when hyperscalers lost ~$900B in a week over AI capex ROI concerns.

Revealed: Federighi stated on the record the Siri delay was a failure to meet Apple's own quality bar, 'not a strategic choice'; the overhaul has slipped ~18 months across three announced dates, and Apple's cumulative 2020-2025 AI spend (~$20B) trails every hyperscaler by an order of magnitude in a pattern predating any 'wait for commoditisation' rationale.

loci.name: lockin-durability-preference-vs-ai-interface
loci.one_line: Is Apple's preference-based retention durable if AI relocates the primary interface away from the phone — and does any strong-form (phone-level) switching evidence from DMA markets exist to test it?
loci.rationale: The contradiction graph resolved two clusters independently and they may conflict: retention is 'structural via preference' (more robust to interoperability mandates), while interface relocation is 'a long-horizon tail'. Preference is preference for the CURRENT interface; if AI moves daily interaction off the device, the moat may not transfer. The CEO transition's audited absence of any stated strategy adds uncertainty. Meanwhile the brief's own natural experiment tests only browser switching; phone-level switching in DMA markets is an audited absence that the deep-inference directive says to push on once more before accepting.
loci.deliverable: (1) A final search for strong-form EU phone-switching evidence since March 2024; if none exists, record the absence with what was searched. (2) Evidence on whether brand preference transfers across interface/device shifts. (3) A committed view on whether the annuity class's durability depends on the interface staying fixed within 2-5 years.

opposing_positions.position: Retention is driven by general brand preference (60.8%) far more than ecosystem-investment switching cost (17.4%), which makes it MORE resistant to DMA-style interoperability mandates than cost-based lock-in would be -- preference is the more durable moat.

Preference is measured against the CURRENT smartphone interface and cannot be assumed to transfer to a new one; Eddy Cue testified under oath that AI is moving fast enough that users may not need an iPhone within a decade, OpenAI acquired Jony Ive's device startup explicitly to build a post-smartphone interface, and the corpus confirms an audited absence of any stated AI/interface strategy from Apple's new hardware-engineer CEO -- so the durability of 'preference' as an asset class depends on an interface-continuity assumption the evidence does not actually establish for the 2-5 year window.
